comments.body:
Review remediation record (2026-08-21) for this ticket's plan — moved out of the description to fit the plan-review admission cap. Five blocking gaps were found and closed; the constraints they produced now live in the description, and this comment preserves the investigation trail.

- The `32767` oracle was wrong. The original AC verified consolidation with `grep -rn "32767\|32000" src/rebar/_engine` "returns one file". That oracle could never pass: `32767` occurs in FOUR files and most occurrences must survive — `adapters/jira/comment_limits.py:41` `_JIRA_COMMENT_MAX_CHARS` (Cloud's limit, in scope), `rebar_reconciler/runtime.py:46` `_DEFAULT_COMMENT_MAX_CHARS` (the runtime default), `adapters/jira_datacenter/settings.py:60,64` (the DC `jira.text.field.character.limit` default-value quoted from Atlassian docs), and `adapters/jira_datacenter/backend.py:244-257` (prose citing JRASERVER-28519 for why 32767 is only a DC default). Deleting those would delete sourced product knowledge. The construct being consolidated is the fit-for-send composition, not the number, so the AC was rewritten to an observable behavioural property: the dedup key is derived from the bytes actually sent.

- Only ONE of two mutation-enactment consumers was in Scope. The plan scoped `_engine/rebar_reconciler/dispatch_one.py:368-379` (create path) but missed `_engine/rebar_reconciler/dispatch_apply_phases.py:375-384` (update path), which is structurally identical — same `entry.get("body", "")` read, same single-attempt `client.add_comment(issue_key, body)`, same `_record_comment_id` follow-up. Leaving it out would have kept the update path sending the un-fitted `body` while the key came from `wire_body`: the exact drift this leaf closes, on half the traffic. Both are now in Scope and both take `entry["wire_body"]` with a pre-cutover fallback to `body` so an in-flight queue does not break.

- The `fit_comment` port and its two implementers were unscoped. `_engine/rebar_reconciler/_backend.py:481` declares `fit_comment(self, body: str) -> str`, contract "return exactly the marker-free body the backend's SEND path lands"; implementers are `adapters/jira/backend.py:154` (Cloud) and `adapters/jira_datacenter/backend.py:303` (DC), both delegating to `outbound_comments.fit_comment_as_sent` (`outbound_comments.py:290`). Decision recorded: `fit_comment_as_sent` is RETAINED as a thin wrapper over `fit_for_send(...).landed_text`, so the Protocol signature and both implementers keep working unchanged and only callers that need the wire bytes move.

- "Adapters only encode and send" was under-specified. Made explicit: `acli_cli_ops.add_comment:531`, `adapters/jira/backend.add_comment` and DC's `sanitize_comment` stop fitting/encoding independently; `wire_body` is carried on the mutation entry so the bytes are computed once; the send path writes `wire_body` verbatim and, where an adapter genuinely must encode at send time, it must receive the SAME codec instance `fit_for_send` was given. A second codec instance, or a second read of the cutover flag, re-opens the drift, so an identity assertion pins it.

- A stale claim in Context, corrected. Context asserted that `codec.normalize_outbound(...)` at `outbound_comments.py:572` is "still an unmatched extra step". That call is no longer there: the region now derives BOTH keys through `_normalize_comment_body` under bug `17c3-2f6e-a5e0-438c` ("BOTH keys must be produced by ONE decoder"), which already closed that specific asymmetry. The remaining gap this leaf addresses is narrower and real — the key PREDICTS the wire the send path will produce, rather than being taken from the bytes actually sent.

- Housekeeping: the original description carried the whole remediation block and the Acceptance Criteria block twice, including the superseded `grep 32767` criterion. The duplicates were removed and the corrected criteria kept.

comments.body:
Implementation record (2026-08-21). The plan passed review at rv10 after one blocking finding was closed and three advisory ones were designed out; this comment keeps the trail.

- The rv9 BLOCK (criterion G6) was a broken acceptance oracle, not a broken plan. AC-1 asserted `key == hash(wire_body)`, but the key is `landed_text` — the marker-STRIPPED decode of `to_wire(wire_body)` — while `wire_body` is the marker-BEARING pre-encode text, so the two can never be equal. AC-1 now states the equality that actually holds and that the Jira-side inbound key is symmetric with: `key == landed_text == strip_marker(decode(what the transport received))`.

- The "one codec, one set of bytes / the send path MUST NOT re-encode" constraint was internally inconsistent and has been replaced. Cloud's wire is JSON-serialised ADF, so `codec.to_wire` MUST run at send time; there is no verbatim-bytes path to have. What must not happen is a fit that MOVES the bytes after the key was taken. The adapters therefore keep their defensive fit (it still covers direct callers) and the leaf pins the property that makes the key sound: re-fitting an already-fitted body is byte-identical, asserted on each deployment's real fitter rather than assumed.

- The third `add_comment` call site — `dispatch_one.py:636`, the illegal-transition status fallback — is deliberately out of scope and is now named as such. It posts a short literal that never passes through the differ and has no `wire_body`; it keeps reaching the adapter's own fit.

- The truncation-suffix literal (three definitions) and the `32767` occurrences were both dropped from scope, and the reasons recorded. `test_rich_text_codec.py:69-71` documents that `adf._ADF_TRUNCATION_SUFFIX` and `rich_text._WIKI_TRUNCATION_SUFFIX` are defined independently ON PURPOSE — "the shared layer must not import the Cloud module" — and pins them to one value; collapsing that is a package-layering decision, not part of this leaf. The `32767` occurrences are sourced product knowledge (the DC `jira.text.field.character.limit` default, cited to JRASERVER-28519), so the earlier grep-count oracle could never have passed. Dropping both also removed the E4/E6 advisories, which were about an oracle (`git diff --stat`) that could not distinguish prose from code.

Implementation: `fit_for_send(body, *, sanitizer, codec, inbound_mapper) -> FittedComment(landed_text, wire_body)` in `outbound_comments.py`; `_diff_comments` keys on `landed_text` (byte-identical to the previous `compare_body`, so the diff decision is unchanged) and puts `wire_body` on the mutation; `dispatch_one.py` and `dispatch_apply_phases.py` read `entry.get("wire_body") or entry.get("body", "")`.

Mutation evidence for the new suite (each mutation applied to the live code path, then reverted; the whole file is green before and after):
- drop `"wire_body"` from the mutation entry -> 12 failures incl. `test_over_limit_comment_converges_after_one_pass` on all four [deployment x path] cases.
- create path stops falling back to `body` -> exactly the two `test_an_entry_without_wire_body_still_sends_its_body[*-create]` cases fail.
- `dispatch_apply_phases` ignores `wire_body` -> exactly the six update-path cases fail; create stays green.
- `fit_for_send` stops decorating -> `test_key_equals_the_marker_stripped_decode_of_what_the_transport_received` and the corpus test fail on the marker assertion.
- `fit_for_send` skips the fit -> the "over-limit body must reach the wire fitted" and idempotence assertions fail, and the corpus test fails on "the wire text must already be fitted".
- the differ keys on the raw body instead of `landed_text` -> the corpus test fails on "a landed corpus body must not be re-emitted".

The first corpus test drafted here was a tautology (it recomputed both sides through `fit_for_send`) and survived every mutation; it was rewritten to three per-body statements — marker survives, wire is already fitted, a landed body is not re-emitted — and now dies under three separate mutations.

compiled_state.description:
## Context / Problem
The outbound Jira comment dedup key is one composition of functions in the differ; the
send is a *different* composition in the adapter. Every convergence bug in this area has
been a point where the two drifted.

Today, at `_engine/rebar_reconciler/outbound_comments.py:591-594`, the differ builds its
key as `_normalize_comment_body(codec.to_wire(_decorate_outbound_comment(
sanitizer.fit_comment(body))))`, but the mutation it appends carries only
`_decorate_outbound_comment(body)` — the **un-fitted** body. The transport then re-derives
the wire independently: Cloud at `adapters/jira/acli_cli_ops.py:531`
(`json.dumps(codec.to_wire(fit_preserving_marker(body, codec.fit_outbound)))`), Data Center
at `adapters/jira_datacenter/backend.py:543` (`transport.add_comment(remote_id,
sanitizer.sanitize_comment(body))`, whose truncate is `fit_preserving_marker(text,
self._fit_raw)`).

So the key **PREDICTS** the wire the send path will produce rather than being taken from
the bytes actually sent, and it is correct only for as long as three separately-maintained
compositions stay in lockstep. `fit_comment_as_sent`
(`outbound_comments.py:290`) exists solely to re-run the send's fit, and each backend's
`fit_comment` (`adapters/jira/backend.py:156`, `adapters/jira_datacenter/backend.py:309`)
documents that it must reproduce its adapter's send composition exactly. That is the
structure this leaf removes.

(The normalisation asymmetry at the same site is already closed by bug
`17c3-2f6e-a5e0-438c`; it is not what this leaf targets.)

## Approach
Add to `outbound_comments.py` (the backend-neutral core — it names no vendor and no
numeric limit, pinned by `tests/unit/rebar_reconciler/test_backend_neutrality.py`):

```
FittedComment = frozen dataclass(landed_text: str, wire_body: str)

fit_for_send(body, sanitizer, codec, *, inbound_mapper=None) -> FittedComment
    wire_body   = _decorate_outbound_comment(sanitizer.fit_comment(body))
    landed_text = _normalize_comment_body(codec.to_wire(wire_body),
                                          inbound_mapper=inbound_mapper)
```

`_diff_comments` calls it once per candidate body: it keys on `landed_text` (byte-identical
to today's `compare_body`, so the diff decision is unchanged) and puts `wire_body` on the
mutation entry alongside `body`. Both enactment consumers then send `wire_body`.

The key is therefore no longer a prediction: it is the decoded readback of the exact string
handed to the transport. `fit_comment` and its two implementers stop being a convergence
obligation and become an ordinary fit, because nothing downstream re-derives the text.

## Constraint: BOTH mutation-enactment consumers are in Scope
Two structurally identical consumers, not one — same `entry.get("body", "")` read, same
single-attempt `client.add_comment(...)`, same `_record_comment_id` follow-up:
- `_engine/rebar_reconciler/dispatch_one.py:368-379` (create path);
- `_engine/rebar_reconciler/dispatch_apply_phases.py:377-386` (update path).

Scoping only one would leave the other sending the un-fitted `body` while the key came
from `wire_body` — the exact drift this leaf closes, on half the traffic. Both read
`entry.get("wire_body") or entry.get("body", "")`, so a mutation entry queued **before**
the cutover (no `wire_body`) still sends.

`dispatch_one.py:636` — the illegal-transition status fallback — posts a short literal
(`local status changed to <status>`) that never passes through the differ and has no
`wire_body`. It is deliberately OUT of scope and keeps reaching the adapter's own fit.

## Constraint: the adapter's fit stays, and must be IDEMPOTENT
The send path is not made encode-free: Cloud's wire is JSON-serialised ADF, so
`codec.to_wire` must run at send time. What must not happen is a fit that **changes the
bytes** after the key was taken. The adapters keep their defensive fit (it still guards
direct callers like `dispatch_one.py:636`), and the property that makes the key sound is
that re-fitting an already-fitted body returns it **byte-identical** — `fit_preserving_marker`
truncates content and re-appends the marker, so a within-limit input is returned unchanged.
That idempotence is asserted directly, on both the Cloud and DC fitters, rather than assumed.

## Constraint: the `fit_comment` port keeps its contract
`_engine/rebar_reconciler/_backend.py:487` declares `fit_comment(self, body: str) -> str`.
`fit_comment_as_sent` is **RETAINED** unchanged as the shared implementation, so the
Protocol signature and both implementers keep working. Only the differ moves to
`fit_for_send`, confining the change to the dedup-key path.

## Out of scope: the truncation-suffix literal
`" … [truncated by reconciler]"` is defined three times
(`adapters/jira/comment_limits.py:46`, `adapters/jira/adf.py:333`,
`adapters/jira_family/rich_text.py:69`). That is a real duplication, but a *deliberate* one:
`tests/unit/rebar_reconciler/test_rich_text_codec.py:69-71` records the reason — "the shared
layer must not import the Cloud module" — and pins the three to one value. Collapsing it is a
separate decision about package layering, not part of deriving the key from the sent bytes,
and is left to its own ticket. The `32767` occurrences under `src/rebar` are likewise
untouched: they are sourced product knowledge (the DC `jira.text.field.character.limit`
default, cited to JRASERVER-28519), not duplication.

## Scope
`src/rebar/_engine/rebar_reconciler/outbound_comments.py`,
`_engine/rebar_reconciler/dispatch_one.py`,
`_engine/rebar_reconciler/dispatch_apply_phases.py`,
`tests/unit/rebar_reconciler/test_fit_for_send.py` (new).

## Testing
Happy path over the captured corpus `tests/fixtures/cloud_adf_corpus/bodies_*.json`: for
every body, `fit_for_send(...).landed_text` equals the marker-stripped decode of
`codec.to_wire(wire_body)`. Edge: an over-limit body keeps `RECONCILER_MARKER` and the key
still matches; a DC body fits at `comment_max_chars()`. Regression pinning (must pass
unchanged): `test_outbound_comment_length_convergence.py`,
`mutate/test_dc_outbound_comment_length_convergence.py`,
`mutate/test_outbound_comment_marker_survives_truncation.py`,
`test_acli_comment_adf_encode.py`, `test_rich_text_codec.py`, `test_backend_neutrality.py`.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [x] The dedup key is the readback of the bytes sent: a test fits an over-long comment,
      drives it through a fake transport, and asserts
      `key == landed_text == strip_marker(decode(what the transport received))`.
- [x] For every corpus body, `landed_text` equals the marker-stripped decode of
      `codec.to_wire(wire_body)`; checked by the new corpus test.
- [x] `landed_text` is byte-identical to the key `_diff_comments` produces today, so the
      diff decision is unchanged; checked by the pinning suites passing unchanged.
- [x] BOTH enactment consumers (`dispatch_one.py` create, `dispatch_apply_phases.py` update)
      hand the transport `entry["wire_body"]`; checked by a test driving each path through a
      fake transport and comparing against `fit_for_send(...).wire_body`.
- [x] Re-fitting `wire_body` returns it byte-identical on BOTH the Cloud and the DC fitter,
      so the adapter's defensive fit cannot move the bytes after the key was taken; checked
      by an idempotence test over in-limit and over-limit bodies.
- [x] A mutation entry written before the cutover (no `wire_body`) still sends its `body`,
      on BOTH paths; checked by a back-compat test.
- [x] `fit_comment_as_sent` and the `_backend.fit_comment` Protocol keep their `-> str`
      contract; checked by both implementers (`adapters/jira/backend.py:156`,
      `adapters/jira_datacenter/backend.py:309`) passing unchanged.

file_impact.reason: new fit_for_send + differ keys on landed_text and carries wire_body
new behavioural tests for the key/wire contract
